historical_commentary.text: This note traces the history and then-current state of how 4th Dimension handles picture data, particularly the added complexity introduced once 4D for Windows required cross-platform picture format compatibility alongside classic Mac picture formats (e.g. PICT); the specific formats and internal handling mechanisms described are tied to 4D v6-era classic Mac/Windows graphics conventions and have been superseded by modern image format support and rendering in current 4D.
related_updates: 4D's picture field/variable handling has been substantially modernized since this v6-era note, with support for a much broader range of contemporary image formats
Classic Mac-native picture formats (like PICT) discussed as historical context here were phased out by Apple well before modern macOS, and 4D's own picture handling has moved on accordingly
